# TerminalMind

Search and browse your entire Claude Code conversation history from a local dashboard.

Claude Code already saves every prompt, message, and tool call to disk. TerminalMind indexes that data into SQLite, gives it AI-generated titles, and serves a browser dashboard so you can find anything you've ever worked on — without digging through raw files.

---

## What it does

**Browse all sessions** — every Claude Code session with a clean title generated by a local AI model (llama3.2 via Ollama, or a smart heuristic fallback). Grouped by Today / Yesterday / This Week / Older. Click any session to read the full conversation inline.

**Search everything** — full-text search across all messages and prompts. Filter by time window. Results grouped by session with highlighted matches.

**Auto project tags** — sessions are automatically tagged by project (Segmentation, SpotTrader, PKB, etc.) based on what you talked about.

**Zero cloud** — all data stays local. Ollama runs on your GPU. No API keys.

---

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+
- [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) installed and used at least once
- Ollama (optional, for better titles) — [ollama.com](https://ollama.com)

---

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/CoderShibay/terminalmd.git
cd terminalmd
bash install.sh
```

Or directly:

```bash
bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CoderShibay/terminalmd/main/install.sh)
```

The installer:
- Checks Python 3.10+
- Installs `fastapi` and `uvicorn`
- Creates a `tm` command in `~/.local/bin/`
- Runs the first sync automatically

---

## Usage

```bash
tm serve                        # open dashboard at localhost:8888
tm sync                         # re-index new sessions
tm search "STAPLE ensemble"     # search from the terminal
tm search "bybit" --last 7d     # filter by time
tm sessions                     # list sessions in terminal
tm status                       # DB stats
```

**Dashboard navigation:**
- Click the **⚡ TerminalMind** logo to go home from anywhere
- **Browse** tab — scrollable session list with titles and tags
- **Search** tab — full-text search. Press `/` to jump here from anywhere, `Esc` to go back
- Click a **project tag** to filter sessions. `✕ clear filter` to reset. Browser back button works.
- Click any **session card** to expand the full conversation inline

---

## How it works

Claude Code writes your data to:

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `~/.claude/history.jsonl` | Every prompt you've sent |
| `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` | Full conversation transcripts |
| `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` | Session metadata |

TerminalMind reads these files, indexes them into `~/.terminalmd/db/terminalmd.db` (SQLite with FTS5), and generates titles using llama3.2 (if Ollama is installed) or a heuristic fallback. Titles are cached — each session is processed once.

---

## Ollama (better titles, optional)

If Ollama is installed and llama3.2 is available, `tm sync` will generate natural-language titles like:

> *Optimizing Tumor Segmentation with AI and MRI Data*

Without Ollama, titles fall back to the cleaned first user message. Either works fine.

```bash
# Install Ollama: https://ollama.com
ollama pull llama3.2
tm sync   # re-generates titles for any untitled sessions
```

Sessions titled by Ollama show a `✦` badge in the dashboard.

---

## Data stays local

- SQLite DB: `~/.terminalmd/db/terminalmd.db`
- No network calls (Ollama runs on your machine)
- Claude's original files in `~/.claude/` are never modified
